# DenialZero: an agentic claims-defender for small-business insurance and B2B vendor disputes
**Claim:** Sub_category: Money & Commerce → Investing & Taxes (adjacent: business financial admin). A mobile app for small-business owners (contractors, clinics, restaurants, e-commerce sellers) that ingests a denied claim, vendor chargeback, or disputed B2B invoice plus the full underlying policy/contract, then autonomously drafts AND files the appeal, escalates through portals, and follows up — targeting the non-medical denial market that consumer health-appeal apps ignore.
**Mechanism / rationale:** Requires two recently-feasible capabilities working together: (1) very-long-context reasoning (1M-token tier — GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro — now holds a 200-500 page policy/contract set in one reasoning step [digitalapplied.com], and effective recall holds to ~600-700K tokens), and (2) computer-use/screen-agents that can navigate carrier and vendor web portals to actually submit. A year ago, context windows that reliably reasoned over a full multi-document policy bundle and agents that could complete a portal submission flow were not production-grade; cross-referencing a specific denial code against a 400-page contract clause was the bottleneck. Revenue path: ~33M US small businesses, reachable beachhead of ~2M owner-operators who file/contest claims and disputes annually; reach ~300K via vertical channels (insurance brokers, trade associations), 1% convert = 3,000 paying at $49/mo or a 25% contingency on recovered amounts → conservatively $1.8M+/yr at subscription, more with contingency.
**Novelty:** Closest competitors — Counterforce Health, Claimable [pymnts.com], FightHealthInsurance — are exclusively consumer medical appeals. Pine/Kudos [19pine.ai] do consumer bill cancellation, not contract-grounded claim adjudication. White space: business-side disputes (commercial insurance, denied warranty/chargeback, vendor SLA breaches) where the "evidence" is a long contract no human reads end-to-end — nobody is doing long-context contract-grounded auto-filing for SMBs.
**Test:** Build an MVP on 50 real denied small-business claims with known outcomes; measure (a) clause-citation accuracy vs. a paralegal, (b) successful autonomous portal submission rate, (c) reversal/recovery rate vs. the historical <1% appeal baseline. Success threshold: >40% recovery on contested cases.
**Assumptions:** Carrier/vendor portals are navigable by computer-use agents without hard CAPTCHA walls; long-context recall stays accurate at the clause level; contingency pricing is legally permissible in target states.
